turns.patient_response: Any time I have to get blood drawn, I go to great lengths to avoid it or sit there in sheer terror the whole time. It has become a major hurdle for me, and I just don't know what to do about it anymore.

symptom_reasoning.S063: The patient experiences an immediate fear response ('sheer terror') whenever they are in the situation of getting blood drawn.
symptom_reasoning.S064: The patient actively avoids the situation ('go to great lengths to avoid it') or endures it with intense distress ('sit there in sheer terror').

turns.patient_response: The fear is mostly about the needle going into my vein, which just feels incredibly dangerous to me now. About a year ago, I actually fainted during a routine blood draw and broke my wrist when I fell. Now, even just thinking about getting blood taken makes me feel light-headed, like I might pass out all over again.

symptom_reasoning.S062: The patient describes a specific, intense fear of needles entering their vein, which aligns with a Blood-Injection-Injury type phobia.
symptom_reasoning.S063: The patient experiences immediate physiological symptoms, such as feeling light-headed, and anticipatory anxiety just by thinking about getting blood taken.

turns.patient_response: It is really just about having blood drawn from my vein because of that awful fall, not regular shots or other medical procedures. In fact, even seeing a picture of a blood draw on a clinic poster triggers my anxiety, and I only canceled my cataract surgery because it required those pre-operative labs.
